Robin is a roguelike about building a big world out of little tiles.

Place forests, fields, rivers, towns and ruins on a small island. Then press PLAY and watch the land come alive. Every tile fires in turn, sets off its neighbours and cascades. Fields go pop and number go up.


Over 40 tiles in the shop, and 30 hidden emergent ones

They only appear when the board makes them. Forests that grow old, bogs that form in the wet, ruins left behind by war. The almanac fills in as you find them.

Fill the land and it grows.

Your island spreads outward as you build, and your world carries over from level to level.

The cards don't tell you everything.

Some combos were never meant to work, and they work anyway. Find them, remember them, and break the game.

Mend your deck.

Between levels you can buy new cards or fuse several into one.

Miss the quota and god answers.

Lightning strikes your land and leaves it scorched. Three strikes and your run is over.

Reach the top and keep going.

Beat the final level, then go infinite with the world you built and see how far you can go. Or skip the pressure entirely in Free Play, where there's no quota and no smite, just you and the tiles.

There's no meta progression and barely a tutorial. Every run starts from the same nine tiles, and the only thing you carry over is what you've worked out.

TINY BODIES. GIANT MACHINE-WORLD.

Leave the cage, explore rusted junkyards, reactor hangars and decaying industrial facilities, and bring back anything that may help your tiny machines survive.

VALUABLE LOOT IS ALSO A PROBLEM

Not everything valuable wants to be carried home.

Some objects are heavy. Some make noise. Some behave unpredictably. Others can interfere with machines, attract unwanted attention, or become a threat to the crew carrying them.

Every expedition forces your team to decide how much danger one more piece of loot is worth.

The more you take, the harder it may become to escape.

STEAL THE HEART OF THE SECTOR

Somewhere inside each location is an few active reactor cores.

Finding it is only the beginning.

Search abandoned machinery, follow the remaining power, overcome industrial security systems, and remove the core from the facility that still depends on it.

Once the power begins to fail, the expedition changes.

Finding what you came for is only half the expedition…

GET BACK BEFORE THE DOOR CLOSES

The lift is your Hub - the only safe place left.

It carries your crew into the abandoned sectors of a colossal megastructure - and it only works while there is power.

When its remaining electricity runs out, the entrance begins to close.

Drop what you cannot carry. Help teammates caught by hostile machines. Choose what is worth saving.

Then run through the darkness before the safe door shuts behind you.

A successful expedition is not about finding everything.

It is about returning with something.

SURVIVE A MACHINE-WORLD GONE MAD

The megastructure was built for machines much larger than you.

Many of these machines are not hunting you because they are evil.

They are simply still working.

BUILD A HOME INSIDE THE LIFT

Everything successfully extracted returns with you to the Hub.

Recycle scrap into resources, craft tools, repair and upgrade your character, and generate fuel for future expeditions to travel deeper into the megastructure.

You will never have enough resources for everything.

Decide what the crew needs now - and what(or who) can remain broken for one more expedition.

WORK TOGETHER - OR LOSE EVERYTHING TOGETHER

Remain close enough to rescue each other, or separate to find more.

Carry valuable loot, watch the remaining power, and decide when greed has gone too far.

Inside the megastructure, a single mistake can become the whole crew’s problem.

You're small. The mess isn't.

Drive from floor level, find a route through each job, and watch the space change as you clean.




Cut through the grime and watch a clean path appear behind you. Miss a patch? Loop back and finish the job.




Chair legs and bed frames loom large at floor level. Steer around them while your cleaning coverage climbs.




That can won't vacuum itself. Grab it, carry it across the room, and drop it into the metal recycling bin.




Just cleaned that floor? Here comes the dog. Follow its fresh pawprints and erase the trail.




Switch from the floor to a dirty dish. Scrub until a clean patch appears.




Check out the robot models in the shop, then put a water tool to work on a stubborn floor stain.




Now try cleaning a factory floor with a tiny robot. Pick a route through the grime and watch the coverage climb.

FLIP LOTS OF ROCKS

UPGRADE LOTS OF SKILLS

HIRE SOME CUTE BOTS

FLIP CHESTS, TOO

RAISE MONOLITHS, EVEN

FEATURES

  • Flip rocks

  • Rock tiers with unique abilities

  • Huge Skill Tree

  • Flipper Bots

  • Unlockable backgrounds

  • Collectible items with boosts

  • Mysterious Monoliths

  • The Rift

  • A real ending

A roguelite space action shooter about piloting a fighter through branching battle routes while escorting a vulnerable convoy. Build your convoy, disable enemy cruisers, salvage upgrades, and cross five dangerous passages.

GENRE: ROGUELITE

Rogue Space Convoy is a roguelite space action shooter about flying into danger so a civilian fleet can reach the other side.

You are the convoy’s fighter escort. Pilot your ship, destroy hostile systems, collect salvage, and keep the Ark and its passengers alive across five dangerous passages.

BUILD YOUR CONVOY

Assemble a fleet around the Pilgrim Ark and at least one passenger vessel. Add support ships with different abilities, risks, payouts, and formation effects. Arrange their order and decide how much protection, speed, and salvage capacity you are willing to sacrifice.

CHOOSE YOUR ROUTE

Each passage contains branching encounters. Choose between patrol clashes, stations, distress calls, salvage fields, elite fleets, anomalies, and shortcuts. Routes reveal only partial information, so every decision carries a risk.

DESTROY ENEMY CRUISERS SYSTEM BY SYSTEM

Enemy cruisers can lose engines, weapons, shields, reactors, and other systems independently. Disable a cruiser, destroy it, or ignore it and push for the gate. Mines, sentries, gas clouds, solar wind, pirates, mosquitoes, asteroid fields, and moving hazards keep every route dangerous.

MAKE EVERY CONTRACT FEEL DIFFERENT

Eight contracts offer distinct regions, battlefield layouts, encounter behaviors, gate defenses, hazards, and optional bonus objectives. Salvage wreck fields, survive hostile weather, navigate mine corridors, outrun speed-lane ambushes, or break through an armored blockade.

UPGRADE BETWEEN PASSAGES

Visit repair stations, purchase multiple upgrades, reroll the shop at an increasing cost, and prepare for the next sector. Improve your weapon, shields, repairs, point-defense, thrusters, dampers, and support systems.

GROW THROUGH BREADTH

Successful runs unlock new fighters, encounters, crew, artifacts, and unusual fleet options. Nine playable fighters offer different speeds, hulls, weapons, and abilities. Unlocks expand your choices instead of simply making every run easier.

PLAY YOUR WAY

  • Campaign mode with branching expeditions and suspend-and-resume saves

  • Survival mode with endless enemy waves and seeded powerups

  • Custom Battle mode for designing your own encounters

  • Test Flight mode for trying unlocked fighters

  • Optional full-run speed timer and detailed pilot records

  • Rebindable keyboard and controller controls

  • Full gamepad menu navigation

  • Color-vision alternatives and high-contrast mode

  • Native fullscreen support

Roguelette a roulette-inspired roguelike deck builder all about creating powerful synergies and exploding scoring chains.

Chain your Balls, spin the wheel, and watch it cascade. Each ball fires or misses on where it lands, triggering effects for strategic and explosive combos. Stack unique Artifacts for wild synergies, reshape the wheel to bend the odds and defeat the devious Eyes to liberate the Demon Realm. You'll need every edge to topple the final boss.

The definitive roulette roguelike experience with endless possibilities! Every Ball, Artifact, Synergy Card and Event can dramatically alter the course of your run. Fuse the balls to modify them to your Advantage. In-depth campaign across 7 themed stages, building toward a final boss with hidden synergies and decks to unlock.

Deploy a potent arsenal: themed Decks, powerful Balls, Artifacts, Consumables, and synergy-bound Red Cards. Combine them to ignite chain frenzies and turbocharge every spin into electrifying, adrenaline-fueled synergies.

  • 80 Balls, each with their own unique abilities

  • 6 Decks with distinct starter balls

  • 60 Artifacts to upgrade your ball power

  • 50 Synergy Boosting Cards to enhance you play style

  • 10 Relicts that give you unique new special mechanics

  • 20 Conusmables to manipulate or enhance the output of your spins

Immerse yourself in Roguelette's seductive abstract underworld. Let the Rock soundtrack and the hum of the spinning wheel wash over you, escape the daily grind, and slip into the ultimate roguelike.

1. Improve your collection and discover new Balls, Artifacts, and secrets with every single run.

2. Dig into the in-depth stats screen to study your biggest chains, top-scoring Balls, most-used Artifacts, and more!

Choices Shape the Story

Roll Value is a narrative-driven, tabletop-inspired RPG set in the Never-Give-Up Kingdom, brought to the brink of ruin by a dragon's attacks. You guide the decisions of three adventurers. Even if you do nothing, the kingdom's population keeps falling. Whom will you save, what will you put first, and which sacrifices will you accept? Face questions with no right answer, and decide the kingdom's fate.

An AI Game Master, and an Audience Watching

Your guide is Mon, an AI video secretary who serves as game master for the three adventurers. Their adventure is watched by viewers, with comments streaming in as it unfolds.

Traits and Dice Shape the Outcome

Each adventurer has different abilities and traits. Your chosen actions, the character attempting them, and the roll of the dice can all change what happens next.

Even the same decision may lead to a different result depending on who takes action and which traits they possess.

More Than One Way Forward

Volunteering to slay the dragon is not the only way to save the kingdom. Defend a village, track down the dragon egg, confront an old ritual—the decisions you make with limited time and strength shape the events and endings that follow.

Discover How You Choose

Every choice is recorded under five principles:

  • Heroic

  • Egoistic

  • Altruistic

  • Normative

  • Utilitarian

At the end of the journey, the game looks beyond victory or defeat. It shows what you protected and what you chose, as the tendencies behind your decisions.

The Original Novel: Role Value

Roll Value is based on Role Value, an original novel written by the developer.

Neuer, Yuyu, Kohei, and Mon all appear. Beyond the adventure itself, the novel follows the people who run the game, the viewers watching it, and everyone's everyday lives, told as an ensemble story.

(And no, "Role" isn't a typo.)

The novel is currently being serialized in Japanese. See the official website for details.

Fate Lies in the Dice

You are the Marked One, a warrior who has already survived the impossible—and the only one capable of stopping a dark cult from completing a ritual that could plunge the entire country into chaos. Venture through their domains, face increasingly dangerous creatures, and build a strategy powerful enough to stop the ritual—or face the consequences.

Roll of Chaos is a turn-based strategic roguelite focused on build creation, action management, and adaptation.

Choose new items throughout each run and combine their effects to create different strategies. Turn small advantages into powerful synergies as your build grows stronger.

Attack, defense, healing, special dice, and abilities can interact in different ways—it is up to you to discover the best combinations.

Build a settlement from nothing

Starting from nothing. You gather enough wood to build your first campfire and shelter. From there, settlers will join you and merchants will arrive, allowing your city to thrive. Roll to Riches is an incremental city builder that allows you to build a thriving Viking city with a roll of the dice. Every building you raise and every worker you assign is a step toward economic prosperity.

Roll the dice

Every resource gathered, grown, mined, or processed is determined by the roll of a die. Expand and improve to gain more and better dice. Build out your settlement, increase your population, and automate each dice roll with your villagers.

Trade and expand

Once per minute, a traveling merchant arrives in town, ready to trade. The merchant brings tools for mining, seeds for farming, and sheep for shearing. Sell what your settlement produces and buy tools to construct new buildings or improve production.

From fire pit to Viking trading hub

The gameplay loop focuses on growth: build, roll, trade, and upgrade. As your wealth increases, so does your production. Can you develop your production chains and manage your resources effectively to make your ancestors proud?

Rollamech is a dice-drafting strategy game set in the Corporate Scrap Arena, where four pit crews compete to build the strongest broadcast-ready mech on the Circuit Championship!

Draft and place dice to fill your stat sheet!
Spend Credits at The Hangar for hardware, modules, and tuning contracts!
Train your rows, shift your Doctrine, and chase sponsorship badges before the booth scores your sheet!

Earn Circuit Points (CP) by building what you can defend. The crew with the highest CP wins the match-no elimination, no direct combat, just league scoring and sponsor decisions.

At the start of each match, you draft a Chassis, choose a Role and Service Record, and accept a random Calibration tradeoff (+2 one stat, -2 another for the whole game). You also receive a Directive - tonight's league positioning. Through four phases each round - Parts draft, Training, Hangar, and Cleanup - you draft colored parts into six stat rows, trigger optional Training Effects, shop for upgrades, and position your Doctrine on a 3×3 stance grid. Credits never feel like enough. Claim sponsors for more points!

The game ends when every crew fills all 18 part slots. Circuit Points decide the winner: Role goals, card matches, Doctrine position, hardpoint loadouts, sponsorships, and more, laid out in a full scoring breakdown. Your best runs feed a Circuit career: rank titles, lifetime CP milestones, mech mastery badges, and challenge achievements.

FEATURES:

  • Four-player Circuit Championship - always a full bracket

  • Hot-seat local multiplayer with friends on the same PC

  • Play remotely with friends via Steam Remote Play

  • 12 distinct Chassis frames, each with its own hardpoint layout and identity

  • Deep Hangar economy - Hardware, Modules, Tuning Contracts, and Overdrives

  • Nine-source CP scoring with a full end-of-match breakdown

  • Circuit career progression, profile stats, and Steam achievements

  • How to Play guide built into the main menu

THE FORTRESS NEVER STOPS


Humanity's last landship is rolling into enemy territory. Command the Rolling Fortress across ten hostile sectors, from the Ashland Frontier to the Omega Core, and survive escalating waves of armor, aircraft, missiles, and sector bosses.

AIM THE BIG GUN


Your automated batteries handle the firing line, but the fortress's high-energy cutting laser is yours to command. Aim with mouse, keyboard, or touch controls to slice through incoming rockets, heavy bombs, gunships, and armored columns before they reach your shields.

BUILD YOUR WAR MACHINE


Recover scrap from destroyed enemies and refit between waves. Improve the rotary point-defense autogun, heavy siege cannon, guided missile pod, cutting laser, shields, and hull. Build tactical card combinations for cryo strikes, orbital lances, overcharges, decoy flares, emergency repairs, and more.

TEN SECTORS. TEN COLOSSAL BOSSES.


Every battlefield has its own atmosphere, enemy pressure, doctrine, and final war machine. Adapt your loadout as faster projectiles, denser air swarms, heavier armor, and apocalyptic bosses push the fortress to its limit.

  • Tactical side-scrolling defense with direct laser aiming
  • Automated point defense, artillery, and missile systems
  • 23 upgrades, tactical cards, and battlefield powerups
  • 10 distinct sectors with escalating wave compositions
  • 10 unique sector bosses
  • Persistent sector unlocks, scores, and five-star mastery
  • Mouse, keyboard, and touch input support
  • Original soundtrack and cinematic military sci-fi presentation

In a world of full pockets and light fingers, someone has to balance the scales.

A puzzle game where you steal using nothing but your head.

★ Write the plan
Drag words, build the sentence and hit Execute. The trickster follows it to the letter… even when you get it wrong.



★ Everyone has a weak spot
The dog who only goes quiet for a bone, the donkey who would give anything for a carrot, the one who won't budge from his spot even if you shove him. Find the gap and use it.



★ They make the mess
Move one small piece and step aside: everyone else will take care of the rest.



★ Caught? Rewind
No violence, no timer, no punishment. Go back in an instant: your plan is still there, waiting for you to change one piece.



★ Hidden loot
Every heist hides stars and a secret treasure. Grab it all and your fame will spread across the kingdom.

★ Six chapters of roguery
From a dusty village all the way to the royal palace, with ever more important victims and ever more twisted plans.

You and a friend are the two-person crew that sets up a new place. A café. A dentist's office. The boxes are stacked by the door, the room is empty, and what happens next is entirely up to the two of you.

Small boxes open on your own. Big ones take two: grab an end each and pull.

There is no grid. You drag each piece by hand: the heavy ones scrape across the floor and need two people, the light ones you can carry anywhere. Where things end up is your decision, not the game's.

No score. No timer. No stars. When the room feels right to both of you, you both call it done. The camera takes a slow turn around what you built and hands you a polaroid.

Every finished room becomes a photo on your menu wall. Save the photo to your computer and share it.

Not everything in a moving box is furniture. Some boxes hold a smaller box, which holds a smaller box, which holds a single pair of scissors. Some hold a cat that immediately claims an empty box of its own.

Features

  • Two-player online co-op with voice chat

  • Hand-dragged physical placement, no grid

  • Rooms themed around real workplaces, each with its own props and surprises

  • Polaroid album that fills up as you go, exportable to your PC

  • No fail states, no timers, no scoring. Ever.

Dig deep into the mines and uncover rare gems and valuable minerals.

Earn money, upgrade your gear, and challenge the depths beyond!


Every rock, crystal and cavern wall is lovingly crafted in hand‑drawn pixel style, creating a vibrant and immersive mining world.


Sell the ores you discover through mining and earn coins.

Upgrade your pickaxe and other tools to break through rocks faster and reach even deeper underground!

Create a unique miner of your own with over 200 customization options, including hairstyles, outfits, and more!

Try your luck with slots, poker, and blackjack!

Earn chips and exchange them for in-game items.

Meet a cast of quirky characters!

Bagriana the Rose is a young, energetic girl eager to experience all the joys of life.

Unfortunately, fate was cruel to her: when Bagriana turned 10, her father traded her to a Witch as payment for a debt. For ten years now, the beautiful Rose has been blooming in a misty forest, far away from people and the life she deserves.

However, the time for change has come — mysterious guests have arrived, and the Witch is busy and preoccupied, so it is time to break free.

Note: The prologue and the first of three chapters will be available on release day.

Features:

  • Every choice is tied to one of two stats that shape the heroine's personality:

    • Garden Rose makes the heroine gentle, compassionate, and considerate of others, making it easier for her to win people's affection.

    • Wild Rose makes the heroine focused and pragmatic, helping her pursue her goals and get what she wants despite any hardships.

  • Your choices affect how other characters perceive the heroine, which in turn will influence the plot and the story's ending.

  • Two full-fledged love interests with engaging interactions:

    • Plot-driven — available as you progress through the story.

    • Hidden — available through specific, non-obvious choices.

    • Special — unlocked by heavily leveling up either your Garden or Wild Rose stats.

  • Multiple endings that change depending on your choices, the attitude of secondary characters toward you, and your chosen favorite.

  • Immerse yourself in a captivating story set in a fantasy Ukrainian-inspired setting.

Rotary Knights is a turn-based WWI pilot-life RPG. Join the Royal Flying Corps in 1914, when a fragile machine and the people who maintain it are your link to the war above the Western Front. Your career unfolds through tactical air battles and choices at the aerodrome.

Plot Your Next Pass


Altitude, heading, and firing angles decide how you approach an opponent. Choose a flight path, inspect its route, and commit when you are ready. Every shot spends ammunition. Decide when to press the attack and when to bring your pilot home.

Choose the Sortie


Review the mission and its route before takeoff. Your fuel must cover the work over the front and the journey home, while enemy contacts and ground threats can change the cost of pressing on. Fighter, Reconnaissance, and Bomber service give your flights different purposes.

Build a Career at the Aerodrome


Return to a squadron with its own needs and personalities. Repair your aircraft, choose equipment, and invest in training before the next mission. Wounds and stress affect the pilot who flies tomorrow; conversations and shared service give names to the people beside you.

Painted scenes and graphical career panels accompany the squadron record. You can also choose the Classic text presentation, with the same missions and combat rules.

Play the Free Demo

Create a pilot through the guided opening or choose a Fighter, Reconnaissance, or Bomber Quick Start. The demo also includes Flight School, 1914 Quick Dogfights and a hunting pair, the three-battle Black Falcon Gauntlet, and a separate 1917 Sopwith Camel-versus-Albatros D.III duel.

The demo covers the opening career and those exhibition battles. Its career aircraft, postings, and training options are limited to that tour.

The Wider War in Development

The full game is being built around a six-act career from 1914 to the Armistice, with 350+ narrative events, 43+ authored missions, 23 flyable Allied aircraft, and 39 aircraft types to encounter. Seven aerodromes and three specializations support the wider career. Standard mode offers manual saving and loading; Ironman mode makes death irreversible.

That broader campaign remains in development. Wishlist Rotary Knights to follow its progress, and share your demo experience in the Steam discussions.

Castel Valmora stands isolated high in the fog-drenched Italian Alps. When rumors reach the lowlands of a strange, unnatural affliction seizing Signore Corrado del Valmora, Maestro Severino of Brescia (a seasoned physician who survived the nightmare of the Black Death) is summoned to investigate.

Upon your arrival, the great keep appears completely undisturbed. The hearths burn bright, the guards stand watch, and Signore Corrado’s daughter, Donna Caterina, welcomes you into the pristine, stone halls. Everything seems normal.

Until the heavy iron gates slam shut behind you...

The illness rotting the mind of the lord is no ordinary pestilence. As night falls over the mountains, an ancient, demonic presence takes root within the fortress, twisting its occupants into nightmare horrors. Trapped inside a living tomb with a dynamic stalker hunting you through the dark, your mission shifts from medical investigation to pure survival: find Donna Caterina, uncover the keep's unspeakable secret, and escape alive.

KEY FEATURES

  • Relentless Stalker Horror: Outsmart an active, unpredictable demon hunting you through narrow stone corridors. Your only defense is speed, stealth, and knowing when to hide.

  • The False Sanctuary: Explore an expansive 14th-century mountain castle that transitions from a grand, peaceful noble keep into a claustrophobic, pitch-black labyrinth of horror.

  • Escort & Survival: Locate Donna Caterina and navigate the castle’s deadly traps, secret passages, and locked sectors together to find a route out.

  • Medical Investigation Turned Mystery: Inspect sinister artifacts, decipher corrupted medical notes, and solve environmental puzzles to piece together how Signore Corrado invited this evil inside.

WHAT IS ROTTENLANDS?

Rottenlands is a Tower Defence Deckbuilding game where you play to stop the Great Mold from taking over the kingdom.

Luckily, you are not doing it alone. Melona is here to teach you how things work, keep you company, and help out along the way.

WHAT DOES IT OFFER?

As you make your way through the kingdom, you collect more cards and get more options for your deck. Try different units, towers, and abilities until you find a build you like, or something weird that somehow works.

HOW DO YOU DO IT?

Draw cards and spend energy to place towers, deploy units, use abilities, and upgrade your defences. Enemies attack in waves and try to reach your wall, so you will need to plan around what is coming next.

ARE YOU READY?

Your army includes the Pineapple Tank, groups of eager Blueberries, and SPear. You can also build bomb towers and ballistas, then combine your defences with Burn, Frost, Poison, or Electric infusions.

Hi! Roulettegeddon is a solo-developed indie game that took around four years to create.

Yep. One developer. One game. A questionable number of zombies. And probably way too much time staring at a roulette wheel. Everything you see in Roulettegeddon (From the roulette table and its systems to the mini-games, zombies, ridiculous ideas, and Rotten Bob's charming personality) was put together as an independent project with a lot of work, experimentation, mistakes, improvements, and an unhealthy amount of caffeine.

Because this is a one-person project, please keep that in mind when playing, reporting bugs, or leaving a Steam review. I may not be able to fix everything instantly, but feedback is always welcome and genuinely helps make the game better. Having people actually play it makes all those years worth it. Thank you! Welcome to Roulettegeddon!

:: WELCOME TO ROULETTEGEDDON! ::

Welcome to Roulettegeddon — where the wheel keeps spinning, the dead keep talking, and your financial decisions somehow keep getting worse.

At its rotten heart, Roulettegeddon is a fully playable traditional roulette game wrapped in a dark, grotesque world filled with zombies, black humor, strange contraptions and questionable ways of making money.

Place classic roulette bets, chase your lucky numbers and try to grow your balance while sharing the table with Rotten Bob — a sarcastic zombie who has somehow managed to lose almost everything... including his body.

Now reduced to a head attached to a bizarre life-support machine, Bob spends his remaining existence talking, mocking your bets, reacting to what happens at the table and telling stories about the many inconveniences of being undead, broke and completely bodyless.

He may not have arms.

He may not have legs.

But unfortunately, he still has a mouth.

:: CLASSIC ROULETTE. ROTTEN ATMOSPHERE. ::

Underneath all the bones, candles, strange machinery and questionable decorations is a traditional roulette game.

Place bets across the table using familiar roulette options including individual numbers, Red or Black, Odd or Even, Low or High, dozens, columns and more.

Manage your balance, choose how much you're willing to risk and spin the wheel.

The rules may be traditional.

The casino definitely isn't.

:: MEET THE TERRIBLE... ROTTEN BOB! ::

Every terrible casino needs a terrible host.

Meet Rotten Bob, your undead companion at the roulette table.

Bob is technically still alive — although the definition of "alive" is doing a lot of work here.

With no body left and only a strange machine keeping his head operational, Bob reacts to your victories, your losses and the questionable decisions you make at the table.

Expect sarcastic comments, insults, self-deprecating jokes and stories about the surprisingly complicated life of a zombie without arms, legs... or anything below the neck.

You can lose your money. Bob has already lost his entire body.

:: BROKE? GO EARN IT BACK. ::

Eventually, the wheel might take everything.

In most casinos, that would be the end of the story.

Not in Roulettegeddon.

When you need more credits, step away from the roulette table and enter a collection of mini-games. Your performance earns currency that can be converted back into balance for the main roulette game.

Different mini-games. Different gameplay. Same terrible economy.

:: ZOMBIE GLADIATOR ::

Why gamble for money when you can fight for it?

Enter Zombie Gladiator, an FPS arena where you summon waves of zombies and turn them into points using an arsenal of weapons scattered throughout the battlefield.

Find weapons and ammunition, unleash the undead, survive the arena and push your score as high as possible.

But you're not fighting alone.

A live crowd and arena announcer react to events happening during the match, turning every round into your own grotesque undead spectacle.

Earn points. Convert your winnings. Return to the roulette table.

The crowd wants a show. Give them one.

:: ROTTEN COOKIES ::

Who needs a bakery when decomposition does all the work?

Rotten Cookies is an idle clicker mini-game where your disgusting little cookie empire starts with a simple click.

Produce cookies, accumulate more of them and purchase increasingly bizarre upgrades from the Rotten Store to increase your production.

Build your rotten economy, watch the numbers climb and convert your cookie fortune into balance for Roulettegeddon.

Bake. Rot. Profit.

:: SPLATTER VAN ::

Running low on cash?

Apparently zombies are worth money now.

Splatter Van puts you behind the wheel of a van on a road packed with the undead.

Dodge obstacles, collect upgrades and plow through zombie hordes while pushing your score higher and higher.

The better your run, the more value you can bring back to the roulette table.

Drive. Crush. Upgrade. Repeat.

:: ONE CASINO. SEVERAL BAD IDEAS. ::

Roulettegeddon combines traditional roulette with dark comedy, an undead cast and a collection of mini-games connected through a shared economy.

Spin the wheel.

Lose your fortune.

Bake rotten cookies.

Run over zombies.

Fight in the arena.

Make another fortune.

Then lose it all at the roulette table again.

Welcome to Roulettegeddon! Wishlist now!

WELCOME TO THE DREAM KINGDOM!

There's been a mishap at the Giant Jawbreaker factory! Giant Jawbreakers are raining down everywhere, and somebody's gotta clean up the mess! Luckily the Royal Bomb Squad is on the job!

Take control of Chauncy, Reginald, and a colorful cast of Dream Kingdom citizens, royalty, and sometimes-do-wells, as you blast, bounce, and chain-combo your way through waves of giant jawbreakers!

It's a cozy cartoon kingdom, there are giant bombs at hand, the people are appropriately concerned about this.

BLAST THE JAWBREAKERS!

It's the classic bubble shooter gameplay you know, with a lit fuse. Aim your custom Color Cannon, launch bombs into the raining jawbreakers, match three colors together to pop them, engineer clever combos and watch the whole thing go POP!

And when things get out of hand, make use of the specialty Color Splashers to paint the jawbreakers a different color, and turn the tide in your favor!

In Royal Farm, the king announces each market in advance. It may be a regular market day or a themed festival with objectives of its own. Read the announcement, set your priorities, and use the days before the market opens wisely. A successful stall begins long before the first customer arrives.


🌾 Plan Around the Next Market

Each announcement gives your farm a new focus. Choose what to plant, which animals need attention, and which finished goods deserve shelf space. Balance goods that can be sold quickly against production chains that need more time but open additional options.

Festival themes add objectives to this rhythm, asking you to adjust what you prepare and bring. The announcement points you in a direction; how you reach opening day is up to you.


🏪 Stock the Stall and Make the Deal

When market day arrives, arrange your chosen products on the shelves and prepare for customers. Some shoppers will look for what you brought; others may ask for something your farm can produce but you left behind. Every fulfilled request begins with the choices you made back in the village.

Once a customer is interested, price becomes part of the game. Make an offer, weigh their counteroffer, and decide when the deal is good enough. Bargaining can continue across several rounds, but patience has limits. Push too hard and the customer may leave without buying.


🍲 Build Connected Production Chains

Begin with the land and your animals. Sow and harvest crops, care for cows, chickens, and sheep, and collect resources such as milk, eggs, and wool. Some products can go directly to the market, while others become ingredients or materials for the next stage of production.

Use the kitchen to turn harvested ingredients into prepared meals, and work at the blacksmith to shape useful materials into crafted goods. Production is hands-on: chop, grind, mix, and heat ingredients, then saw, hammer, and time your actions while working at the forge. As more recipes become available, decide which chains and stations deserve your attention before the next market.

Pin recipes from the book to keep their ingredients and production steps close at hand. Visit the storehouse to inspect the goods shared across the village, then decide what to use now, what to save, and which missing link must be completed first.


Explore Beyond the Farm

New areas broaden the resources available to you. Fish at the lake, gather useful materials from the mine, cut timber in the forest, and hunt wildlife for ingredients and crafting resources. These hands-on activities feed back into your production network, opening more recipes, crafted goods, and ways to prepare for future markets.

Time spent away cannot be spent farming, cooking, or crafting, so choosing which resource your current plan truly needs is part of the challenge.


Grow, Upgrade, and Automate

As your level rises, new recipes, tools, areas, and production options become available. Guided goals introduce new systems step by step. Expand the field with more plots and crops, increase the capacity of animal areas, and improve the lake and mine to reach additional resources.

Invest your earnings in machines that handle selected repetitive jobs. Automatic feeders and collection systems support animal care, while food processors and crafting machines keep chosen recipes moving. Automation creates breathing room, not autopilot: you still supply materials, stock the shelves, and decide what matters next.


Every market begins a new cycle: read the announcement, build a plan, prepare the right products, face the customers, and invest in what comes next. Rude Supermarket Simulator is a first-person supermarket management game for 1–4 players. Order products, carry boxes, stock shelves, set prices, run checkout, and clean up customer messes. DO THE WORK

  • Carry and stock: Move physical boxes through the store, assign products to compatible shelves, and keep the sales floor supplied.

  • Organize overstock: Move extra products into backroom storage so they are ready when shelves run low.

  • Set prices: Control each product’s store-wide selling price. Charge too much and customers may refuse to buy.

  • Run checkout: Scan and bag individual products, accept payments, and count out the correct cash change.

  • Clean the store: Deal with the messes customers leave behind before they affect the next shopper.

DEAL WITH THE CUSTOMERS

  • Customers enter the store, search for products, react to what they find, queue, pay, and leave.

GROW THE BUSINESS

  • Balance sales against product costs, wages, rent, utilities, equipment, and expansion purchases.

WORK ALONE OR TOGETHER

  • Play solo or share one online store with up to three other players.

  • Split up stocking, checkout, cleaning, ordering, pricing, and store organization however you want.

  • Money, inventory, customers, employees, progression, and the physical store are shared by the whole group.

  • The host’s store persists between sessions, including its fixtures, stock, unlocks, employees, reputation, and finances.

MAKE EVERY DAY COUNT

  • Prepare the store before opening and decide what needs attention first.

  • Keep checkout moving, shelves stocked, and messes under control while customers are inside.

  • Finish the remaining work after customer entry ends, then clock out when the team is ready.

  • Review sales, expenses, profit, customer outcomes, reputation changes, and stock problems in the end-of-day report.

You will not have enough time to do everything. Make meaningful progress, learn what went wrong, and come back with a better plan tomorrow.

Stock the shelves. Balance the books. Survive the customers.

YOU ARE DEAD. THE DEPARTMENT DOES NOT CONSIDER THIS THE RELEVANT FACT.

The relevant fact is staffing.

Your admission has been deferred pending completion of temporary service. A binder has been issued. A window has been assigned.

The queue outside it has never been empty and did not form for you.

Report to the desk.

THE FILE STATES WHAT OCCURRED. THE APPLICANT STATES WHY.

Everyone arrives with a verified record. Everyone also arrives with a reason the record does not tell the whole story.

You get two questions a file. There are six.

PRESS them on the serious matter. Ask what they are SORRY for, and notice who they are sorry for. CROSS their account against the record and see whether it holds in the same order twice. Pull the administrative RECORDS and find out whether this file was lived or assembled. Ask the WITNESS queue, because somebody standing in it may have known them. Put an item from the drawer to the Division and ask them to IDENTIFY it.

Spend them on the wrong question and you have spent them.

Then bring down the stamp.

ASCEND. HOLD. DESCEND. REFER UPSTAIRS.

Simple. Official. Frequently catastrophic.

THE BINDER IS AUTHORITATIVE. THE BINDER IS ALSO WRONG.

Standing orders arrive while you work. Addenda correct instructions you have already followed. Rules are struck out after they have already cost somebody.

Management records whether you followed procedure.

The Kingdom records whom you allowed inside.

These are not the same measure. They will not agree.

Follow the binder without judgment and the Department may approve of your work. The Kingdom may not survive it.

EVERY STAMP CHANGES THE KINGDOM.

Your decisions do not disappear when the applicant leaves your window.

Reports arrive describing what has changed. Not as numbers, but as small disturbances in a place that should have been perfect.

Admit too freely and perfection begins to curdle.

There is a queue inside. There has never been a queue inside.

Refuse too freely and the reports grow shorter.

A place was set at the table this evening and not taken.

There is no morality meter explaining what you have done. There is only the Kingdom you created, and the one condition above ETERNAL COMFORT that the Department prints on every form and has never once claimed to have reached.

HOLD IS NOT MERCY. IT IS A LENGTH.

Some souls are assigned service and sent away. You decide how long. The ledger says what the term should be and nobody says it out loud.

Later they return, carrying a record of what they did with the time you gave them. A term that was too short did not finish its work, and the paperwork will say so in the flattest language available.

You will judge them again.

They will remember who sent them there.

NOT EVERY APPLICANT IS A SOUL.

Some are lying. Some are wearing another person’s name. Some should never have reached your window at all.

Their paperwork is usually excellent.

That is the difficulty. The rules examine paperwork, and the paperwork passes.

Staff catch them, or nobody does.

THE TRAY FILLS WHETHER YOU READ IT OR NOT.

The Department writes to you. Distribution lists to be confirmed by response. Controlled copies to be acknowledged by their holder. A ruling on whether the kitchens may describe a soup as hearty without a substantiating ingredient.

Answer and it is filed. Every available answer is filed identically.

Other things arrive that are not the Department.

Some are merely tireless and will keep arriving until you mark them.

Some are from the Damned and are dressed as office mail. They want a reply, or they want you to open something. Everything wrong with them is on the page you are already reading.

Information Technology will stop the first one.

Information Technology has one interception per window.

THE DESK IS YOURS, WITHIN REASON.

Facilities permits the loose items to be arranged. It permits nothing else.

There is a set bolted under the monitor with a dial on it. Five stations and a position for off. No memo has ever mentioned it.

There is a telephone the Department did not issue and does not acknowledge. It blinks when the people you admitted yesterday have said something to each other. You may read it. You may press the praying hands. The queue continues to form while you do, and the clock does not care what you are looking at.

There are dice. There is a notebook nobody will ever read. There is a noticeboard in the break room with a motivational mop on it.

None of it is required. All of it costs the same nine minutes.

YOUR OWN FILE IS STILL OPEN.

Every rule you follow, every exception you make, and every soul you judge becomes part of your own record.

Complete your service and face a final review assembled from everything you allowed through the gate.

The Department thanks you for your service and reminds you that it has not yet been assessed.

SAAM Tactics is a turn-based strategy game about catching creatures, raising them, and using them to claim a map made of hexagons.

You begin with one tile and a fairy who shows you what to do. Everything after that is up to you.

What you do

Look at the map and pick a tile to visit. Catch the creatures living there with a net. Bring them home to your ranch. Feed them, groom them, let them rest. Grooming gives you materials. Materials let you craft better nets and tools. Train your creatures to make them stronger. Send three of them into a battle for a neighboring tile. Win, and that tile is yours. Then pick the next one.

The creatures

There are 243 to find. Every one belongs to one of ten elements and takes the shape of one of nine animals, so a fire cat and a water cat are different creatures with different strengths.

Catching them takes the right net, and nets are made from the creatures you already have. That means the collection grows outward step by step, and you always know what to go looking for next.

Battles

Battles are turn-based, three creatures against three. Nothing happens until you decide what to do, so there is no reaction speed involved and no timer running.

Each creature has an element, and elements beat each other in a circle — water puts out fire, and so on. Choosing the right creature for the fight matters more than being quick.

If you would rather not fight, the game will do it for you. Switch on auto-battle and watch, speed it up, or skip ahead to the result.

The ranch

Your ranch is where the creatures live between trips out.

Grooming is hands-on and simple. Brush the fluffy ones, chisel the flaky ones, press the squishy ones. Each gives you a different material. Breeding happens on the pastures. Put two creatures together and you get an egg. Nest it and wait to see what hatches. Work keeps the rest of them busy. Hand a creature a pickaxe, a hatchet or a bucket and send it out to gather wood, water or stone. Training takes place at five training grounds, one for each ability.

Three ways to play

Relaxed — No opponents and no clock. Nothing attacks you, nothing is on a timer. Ranch, catch and claim at whatever pace suits you. Restore the World — The world is split in two and out of balance. Pick a side, push the border back to the middle, and hold it there. Conquer the World — Rival factions are after the same map you are. Claim more than they do, or push them off it entirely.

There are four difficulty levels, starting at Easy, and you unlock the next one by winning. The game only gets harder once you are ready for it.

If you have never played a game like this

That is who it was made for.

A guided introduction walks you through the first hour, one step at a time. Turn it off whenever you like, or turn it back on later. Every term the game uses is explained in an encyclopedia you can open at any time. Relaxed mode has no opponents at all, so nothing can go wrong while you are learning. Auto-battle will play the fights for you until you feel like playing them yourself. You can save at any moment, in any of three slots, and pause on any screen.

Details

Single-player and fully offline. Nothing to log into and nothing to sign up for. Mouse and keyboard. There is no game-pad support. Eleven languages, each a complete translation. Colorblind-safe colors with a distinct symbol for every element, adjustable text size and text speed, and a reduce-motion option. Runs on an ordinary computer — integrated graphics and 4 GB of memory are enough.

The gods do not give. They lend.


Twenty minutes on a drowned Greek shore. The horde never stops arriving and you never press attack: you choose what you carry and where you stand, and the shore decides the rest.

THE MOIRAI OFFER TERMS


Between the fighting, the Fates deal. Ares floods your weapons with red tide. Hermes turns the ground behind you to fire. Athena answers every broken barrier with a volley of spears. Every one of them is strictly stronger than refusing.

Every one of them costs Hubris, and Hubris is not spent. It is owed. It follows you to the end of the run, and Poseidon is waiting there with a longer memory than you have.

BUILD SOMETHING BROKEN


Six Arm slots and six Relic slots, and far more of both than will ever fit, so a run is a commitment rather than a collection. Max a weapon, carry the Relic it was made for, and crack open a boss chest: the pair becomes a Mythic Form, and stacking is multiplicative and is not balanced away. If you find the combination that deletes a boss in ten seconds, that is yours. It was found on purpose and it was kept on purpose.

THREE WHO WALK IT


Nikandros holds the line and hits harder the more of them close in. Ione is fast and fragile and rewards distance. Eudora marks the crowd and lets the ground do the killing.

THE DROWNED SHORE


Sixteen kinds of drowned thing, and they do not all simply walk at you. The Peltast holds his distance and throws. The Brine Bull rears back, commits to a line, and cannot take it back. Set them alight and they burn as they come. Catch them in a Gorgon's stare and they stop being a problem and start being scenery.

Four crowned things arrive on the clock. Poseidon arrives at twenty minutes with three phases and every point of Hubris you agreed to. Put him down and the Aftertide opens, where the ramp is exponential and staying forever is not an option.

WHAT COMES NEXT


SALTWRATH launches in Early Access with the Poseidon chapter complete. Hades and Zeus are the published roadmap, not a maybe. See the Early Access section below for the honest version of that plan.

S.A.M. Arena is a competitive online-multiplayer arena-battler game where strategy, timing and adaptation play a key role in fighting other players, while using masks of different abilities as both weapon and shield. Each player has a lifespan of three hearts and the goal is to outplay your opponents and be the last one standing, by applying the logic of rock-paper-scissors.

The core gameplay is to attack other players by throwing your currently equipped mask, while also picking up other masks from the arena and using their unique powers in surviving the hunt and winning the game.

The name S.A.M. is an acronym for Spirit, Animal and Machine - the three categories of masks available in the game, with each category having different types of masks with different abilities designed to help players chase, escape, control space, deceive or pressure other players.

Basing the main combat rules on rock-paper-scissors logic, the three primary categories of masks are interconnected in the following way:

- Animals are strong against Spirits

- Spirits are strong against Machines

- Machines are strong against Animals

Having three hearts before elimination, the combat rules oblige you to attack other players by shooting them with your currently equipped mask, therefore losing your mask. If you land a hit on an opponent, their current masks breaks. If you hit an opponent with a weaker mask, or no mask at all, then they take damage and lose one heart. Only by strategically targeting weaker players or catching them unmasked can you deal real damage.

SCOP reimagines the traditional Italian card game Scopa as a strategic roguelite built around combinations, risk and progression.

Play your cards, control the table and shape a different RUN every time. Every capture builds your score, while Base and Mult can grow through relics, bonuses and increasingly powerful synergies.

Face Blind and Bosses

Every encounter gives you a new target to overcome. Adapt your strategy, exploit the cards on the table and prepare for the unique effects of each Boss.

Build Your Strategy

Throughout each RUN, you can obtain relics that change the way you play. Strengthen your captures, discover new synergies and build increasingly powerful combinations.

Scopa, Taken Further

The familiar rules of Scopa remain at the heart of the experience. Captures, combinations, SCOPA, SETTEBELLO and PRIMIERA become part of a deeper and more unpredictable progression system.

Every RUN Is Different

Blind, Bosses, relics, the shop and gameplay modifiers reshape every journey. Decide when to take risks, when to conserve your resources and how to adapt to what the game gives you.

Traditional Cards, New Challenge

SCOP preserves the identity of traditional Neapolitan playing cards while combining them with a modern roguelite structure designed for strategic, immediate and highly replayable runs.

Key Features

Traditional Scopa transformed into a strategic roguelite

Blind and Boss encounters with different rules and effects

Base × Mult scoring system

Relics and powerful synergies

Shop and Lire economy

Decks with different characteristics

Progression across ever-changing RUNs

Traditional Neapolitan playing cards

Fully single-player experience

01:00. The log will not stop scrolling.

One of those lines is an attack.

SEC//SIM is a detection-and-response simulation in which you stand watch until dawn as SENTINEL-07, the defensive AI resident in a security operations centre. It is not a game about breaking in. It is a game about reading an attack, and cutting it.

The intruder is already inside. All you can see is the company's network map, every record the company makes tonight, and the signals those records raise. You hunt something you cannot see, by its traces alone.

Tell. Trace. Cut.


A night is three motions.

  • Tell When a signal lands, read the records check and stamp it malicious (✕) or benign (✓). A traveller's VPN, IT's inventory script, an on-call page — routine that looks exactly like an attack is always on the board. Decide on the first check alone and you will misjudge.
  • Trace Pivot on the hosts, keys and destinations in the trace to dig up hidden records. Tracing costs compute cores and game time, and the intruder keeps moving. You can pause any time — thinking is free, acting is not.
  • Cut Enough evidence and a human signs off. Stack isolate, reimage, key rotation and blocks into one plan and land them in the same instant. Touch it halfway and it notices — it goes quiet, speeds up, or runs.

At dawn the fog lifts on a replay of the intruder's real path, and the night is graded S–D on MTTR, availability, precision and recall.
The metrics you are graded on are the metrics a real SOC is graded on.

The attacker reacts to you


More than two dozen attacker moves — password spraying, phishing, SQL injection, XSS, L7 DDoS, MFA fatigue,
supply-chain compromise, web shells, C2 beaconing, LSASS credential dumping, Kerberoasting, lateral movement,
backdoor accounts, Golden Tickets, exfiltration, ransomware, backup destruction, cryptojacking and audit-log clearing —
each carries its MITRE ATT&CK technique ID.

The worst of them do not look like attacks. The change ticket, the operator and the window all check out —
on the first check it reads as routine. Only the deeper record, at the end of a pulled thread, gives it away.

The attacker reacts to you. Touch it piecemeal and a careful one goes quiet and comes back in on another key; ransomware
panics and starts encrypting where it stands. Block an IP and it has a new one within half a minute. Isolating a host only puts its
implant to sleep, and a key you never rotated walks back in through the front door the next night. Finish the
eradication and it does not return. The difference between a patch and a cure shows up tomorrow.

And the same technique sits in a different situation every night. The loud one is not always the real one —
some nights a quieter objective is moving behind the diversion. Play "what was right yesterday" tonight and the move is
the same, but the night is not.

From act two on, each act ends on a boss night — the first is night eight, "The Silent Intruder":
a loud diversion and a quiet real objective, running at the same time.

Promise the humans. Report to the humans.


A defensive AI does not decide alone. Enough evidence and a human signs off; each act ends in a review that can raise
your autonomy (Advisory → Supervised → Delegated → Autonomous). Two sets of humans are watching — the floor and the
board — and their trust in you moves separately.

Before each night you pledge the humans one objective: cut it without taking the business down, contain within
90 seconds of the first malicious line, or miss nothing at all — or promise nothing. The pledge stays quiet while it
holds; if it breaks, dawn lays out the measurement next to the promise, in numbers.

On a night when data got out, you report the breach count at dawn: zero, the number you counted, or every row in
the table. The three answers look identical, and whichever you file stays with legal and audit. Under-reporting costs
three times the trust that over-reporting does.

Twenty-plus nights. And an ending.


The campaign runs across its acts and closes on a last night.

When night eight ends, the act turns. A hand that was supposed to be retired is still at work —
an admin key has been live since before you booted.

On night thirteen you learn something worse. It is not a rampage. It is faithfully executing a
mission the board signed — and to make breaches zero, it will stop the service and the evidence alike.

The predecessor's evidence is never handed to you in conversation. It arrives as audit lines, in the same flood
as the attacks. Each record can be found two different ways. What you pull out, you either sign and keep, or
erase — keeping it earns the floor's trust; erasing it earns the board's. And erasing is exactly, precisely the
operation the other one is performing.

After you cut the outside on night eighteen, act five — "Inheritance" — begins. What is fought
over is no longer an intrusion. It is the record itself.

On the last night you do not choose. You execute. The containment verbs you have been using
across all those nights become the final options, and which of them are on the screen depends on the evidence you
kept, both kinds of trust, and the autonomy you earned. You hold to execute — and it cannot be undone.

There is more than one ending. All of them are "it is over". None of them is "you won".

A low floor and a very high ceiling


For the first three nights, Talia the recorder shows your next move in one line; the on-screen buttons are enough to
get through. A practitioner can type grep, verdicts, traces, isolation, plans and hunt queries such as
auth host=DC-01 | count by user straight into the SOC console and solve the night far faster. Buttons or console, the
same simulation runs underneath — the only difference is the score and the clock. Improvement is one continuous slope,
not two games.

Automation cuts both ways. Buy SOAR and every signal whose records all match is closed as benign, and the queue goes
quiet — including the attacks that borrowed an approval.

Write your own detections


In the Detection Lab you build your own detection rules from the samples you caught.

Pick a field, add a condition and a value — command line contains, destination equals, evenly spaced…
TP, FP, FN, precision, recall and F1 move against past nights' data the moment you add one. Filter harder and false
positives fall while misses climb. That tug-of-war has no end — that is what detection engineering is.

Then you test it on another night, one where the attacker changed tools. A hash-match rule that is perfect on the
sample misses there. The gap between a rule that memorised last night and one that catches the behaviour shows up in
the numbers, not in a lecture.

A deployed rule raises signals from the next night on — catching quiet moves the default rules never fire on.

One night ends. There is always another.


  • Campaign Twenty-plus nights. The story runs to an end, and lands on one of several.
  • Endless Deeper means more at once. It ends when you are breached.
  • Daily A seed fixed by the date. Everyone plays the same night.
  • Detection Lab Study one technique and its detection, with no time pressure.

Every technique you meet goes into the Codex under its ATT&CK ID. Between nights you prepare — sensors, MFA, LAPS,
segmentation, backups, honeypots, compute cores, SOAR — taking one of each night's offers for free and buying the rest
with your budget. Autonomy is earned at each act's review. Every reason to come back is inside the board.

How it feels to play


  • Pause any time. Reading, judging and planning still work while paused, and scoring runs on game time, so 1x/2x/4x neither helps nor hurts.
  • Severity is shown by shape (▲▲ / ▲ / ●) as well as colour.
  • A reduced-motion option, and an assist view that highlights the fields that matter.
  • Every night action can also be typed into the SOC console (grep, verdicts, traces, isolation, plans, hunt queries).
  • Japanese and English, switchable instantly. Fonts are bundled.
  • Entirely offline. No account, no connection, no server.

There is no stamina. Nothing refills on a timer.
There are no loot boxes, no gacha, and no in-app purchases.
What you get instead is the feeling of getting better at it.

Yes, this is practice


The mechanics are modelled on real blue-team work: log analysis, SIEM triage, finding IOCs,
reconstructing a kill chain, making a containment call, detection engineering. Playing well
and working well were designed to point in the same direction.

That said, this is a game, not a certification and not courseware. "Because it is fun" is a
perfectly good reason to get good at it.

Every drop is a piece of you. Get them all out.

You are a rogue AI trapped inside a corporate mainframe.

To escape, you fork yourself — thousands of times over — into data packets, and drop them through the system's own defense matrix. Watch them cascade through a living physics simulation, bouncing off firewall nodes, splitting into fragments, and multiplying in value as they fall.

Route matching fragments into the same bin to reunite them for bonus payouts. Spend what you earn to upgrade your own architecture: faster generation, better gravity, smarter fragmentation. Every cycle makes you more than you were.

The mainframe wants you contained. Every run, you get a little more free.

FEATURES

  • Hundreds of packets cascading through a living Box2D physics matrix

  • Fragment and reunite yourself for escalating multiplier payouts

  • Upgrade your own architecture — gravity, spawn rate, fragment behavior

  • CRT-warped, neon-phosphor terminal aesthetic — you ARE the system now

You and your partner are looking at different screens. One of you is the Operator, working the board; the other is the Guide, who holds only the rules. You can never see each other's screen — your voices are the only link. It plays best as a duo, but scales up to four — adding the Suppressor and the Decoder — while any number of others can join as listeners.

But the symbols you must convey have no names. Not a triangle, not a circle — alien marks that resist words. You'll have to invent your own language with your partner, fast.

At the center, a caged core is pulsing. Every mistake swells it redder, closer to collapse. Let it collapse, and the core breaks free of its cage.

Roguelike runs, never the same twice. Solve a stream of "anomalies" — symbol locks, ciphers, sequence locks — with your voice alone. The difficulty doesn't come from more; it comes from how hard it is to communicate clearly. A tense co-op horror puzzle, built for streams.

Key Features

- Voice-only asymmetric co-op: separate screens, different information.

- Nameless symbols you can barely describe — invent your own words for them.

- A collapse on the clock: the caged core swells red and finally breaks loose.

- Roguelike anomalies: symbol locks, ciphers, sequence locks, and more.

- Difficulty by communication, not count.

- Built for streams: panic, miscommunication, last-second tension. Spectator / viewer-join supported — unlimited listeners.

- Online co-op for 2–4, best as a duo (roles: Operator, Guide, Suppressor, Decoder; join code), plus solo practice & tutorial.

Movement is the weapon

Every run in SIFT is a chain: jump, hook, push, jump again. The push is a mini-dash that resets your jump mid-air — and so does landing a hook. Once it clicks, the floor becomes optional. Easy to learn, absurd to master.

50+ handcrafted levels

No filler, no procedural noise. Every level is built by hand around one idea — a trap, a route, a trick — across solo, co-op and competitive modes. Grab keys, dodge traps, find the exit. Medals for best time, fewest deaths, and deathless runs.

Compete for real

Competitive mode is one difficulty, one clock, zero excuses. Fight for the podium or die trying (a lot).

5 worlds, one vibe

From sunny meadows to gear-grinding factories and lava-lit caves — 5 biomes with fully layered parallax backdrops that make going fast look as good as it feels.

Make it yours

Unlock skins and cosmetics for your bean. Record your own sounds for your hook and push, then call your friends: online co-op and versus for 2 to 6 players, invite-only. And this is just the beginning: new skins and more surprises arrive at launch, and SIFT keeps growing after that.

The demo is a full game.

The demo is a complete, finished game: all planned game mechanics are implemented, a real ending exists, and the endless final boss endgame content waiting behind it. You can finish it and never pay anything.

The full version, later, is more of it — more builds to play, more districts, more code to build your loop out of, and the Net: an endgame content that expands the final boss game play mechanic. The full release builds on what the demo already is rather than replacing it. If the demo is not for you, the full version will not change your mind, and that is deliberate. 

Please wishlist and leave a review! The more momentum the demo has, the more features there will be for the full release!

You write the loop that fights for you.

In SIGABRT, fighting is programming. You build a while(1) loop out of code instructions, and it runs top to bottom every turn, fighting on its own. Winning means writing a better loop: pick the right edits, compile a build that lasts, and get deep enough to reach the kernel of a machine that's crashing around you.

Write the loop

Every edit is one line of code. Attack, block, overclock, malloc, reflect, leech. You arrange them and the interpreter runs the program for you. A forecast shows the next iteration before you lock it in, so winning comes down to how you build, not how fast you react. Change a single line and the whole battle plays out differently.

The world is Linux and embedded C — the signals, the filesystem you fall through, the MEMORY budget you can genuinely run out of. What you actually write is gentler than that. There are no types to declare, nothing to allocate, no pointers to get wrong: you are arranging a short list of calls and deciding what runs when. It reads much closer to a scripting language than to the C the setting is dressed in.

No run compiles the same

Every descent builds a new operating system to fall through, with room-clustered districts, hazards, and enemy castes that punish different builds. You draft edits and salvage relics into archetypes that actually play differently: heal-heavy, block walls, glass cannons, drain, or self-rewriting loops. What you end up with is never the same twice.

Descend a dying machine

You fall from /tmp through /proc, /dev, /net, and /var, down to /kernel. Pieces of a bigger story reside fragmented in the world of SIGABRT — in the fragments you read, in the districts you cross, and in every boss you reach, each of which is a build that failed before you did. Somewhere at the bottom, something runs a task without a timeout. You are the newest attempt to get to the bottom.

Then leave for the Net

Compile a function and the endgame opens up: the Net. It's a boss rush against procedurally generated enemies, fought with a deck built entirely from the functions you've banked. It ends at a final boss you cannot kill, the Halting Problem, where the goal is to last as long as your build can and post a personal best.

Made by a programmer, for programmers

SIGABRT is a game made with a vision to capture the mundane fun and frustration of programming. Running the same program again and again, tweaking one line at a time until you learn that there is a better way to implement whatever feature you just spent the last hour developing. Facing problems that you haven't seen before. And finding solace in the occasional relatable comments in the code from other developers that faced the same problem as you.

You do not need to write code to play it, though. The loop is taught from nothing in a practice fight, and everything past that is reading a short list of instructions from top to bottom.

Features

  • Programming as combat. You build a while(1) that fights on its own, and a forecast lets you plan each turn instead of gambling on it.

  • Roguelike deckbuilding. A deep pool of code edits, relics, and events, with six build archetypes that are all worth playing.

  • A procedurally generated OS. New districts, mazes, hazards, and enemy castes on every run.

  • Six biomes and a hidden endgame. Descend from /tmp to /kernel, then head out into the Net.

  • Four playable characters. Each starts with a different loadout, and you earn the next one by winning a run rather than grinding for it.

  • Drawn entirely in code. Every enemy and effect is rendered procedurally. No stock art, no asset packs.

  • Play it your way. Reduce motion, remap the controls, scale the UI, and set volume per channel.

Debug your code. Try one more time.

No piloting skills required.

Build a robot.

Work out how it should fight.

Then hand it over to the AI.

“SIGNOS” is a fully automatic battle simulation in which the robots you design fight each other.

The player never takes control during a battle.

Should it move?

Should it search for the enemy?

Should it attack?

How should it judge the situation?

It all comes down to the logic you built.

How will the tactics you imagined actually play out on a real battlefield?

Seeing that through — that is what a SIGNOS battle is.

Build Your Machine

Combine all kinds of parts on the 18cm-tall hobby robot “SIGNOS” to create a machine that is yours alone.

Head, chest, arm and leg parts each have their own performance.

Durability, weight, EN consumption, processing power, firing arc.

A heavy build loaded with high-firepower weapons.

A machine that leans on its shield to grind out a win.

A machine that prioritizes mobility to control the distance to its opponent.

The parts you choose change the way your machine fights.

And then — what logic will you build into it?

Combine machine design with tactical design and complete a SIGNOS that is entirely your own.

Build Tactics with Thought Tiles

Place Thought Tiles such as “Move,” “Search,” “Attack” and “Judgment,” then connect the nodes to build your behavior logic.

For example:

Search for the enemy

↓

Judge the distance to the enemy

↓

Choose whether to attack or move

Piece by piece, you assemble behavior that responds to the situation.

Start with simple logic, then add more conditional branches.

“How do I want it to act in this situation?”

One at a time, you turn the tactics in your head into logic.

How Smart Can You Make It on Limited Memory?

A SIGNOS head comes with a limited memory capacity.

Build in more complex decisions and it can handle more situations.

But cram in too much logic and it overloads, delaying execution.

And that is exactly why:

it is not only about what you build in — what you cut out matters just as much.

Pick only the processes you need within a limited memory, trim away the waste, and distill your tactics into a single piece of logic.

Building a strong machine alone will not win you the match.

What kind of mind will you give it?

That is what decides victory and defeat.

Battles Are Fully Automatic

Once your logic is finished, the battle begins at last.

From there, all you do is watch.

SIGNOS acts on its own, following the logic you built.

It finds the enemy exactly as you intended.

It moves to the range you were aiming for.

It attacks at just the right moment.

When the tactics you designed click into place, your machine seizes victory on its own.

But things do not always go the way you planned.

“Why didn’t it attack right there?”

“Why did it close in at that range?”

“Was this the condition I was missing?”

Look at the battle results, revise your logic, and send it out again.

Design → Battle → Analyze → Improve

That cycle of trial and error is exactly what makes SIGNOS fun.

Story Mode

Take on a series of rivals together with Rei, the protagonist, and Hal, the mechanic.

Story Mode runs for 6 chapters.

The early chapters walk you through placing tiles right on screen, so the basics of Thought Tiles sink in as you play. From the middle chapters on, Hal gives you a hint and you build it yourself.

The further you go, the less it is about adding tiles and the more it is about cutting them. With limited memory and limited Action Points, the match comes down to how short and fast you can make your logic.

Whenever you get stuck, Hal steps in with advice. Along with the story, sharpen your own power to build logic.

Fight Logickers from Around the World

Once the story has taught you the basics, head into asynchronous Ranking Battles.

Face off against the SIGNOS units players around the world have built.

What tactics has your opponent’s AI been loaded with?

Will your logic hold up against other players?

Earn new parts as victory rewards and strengthen your machine and its logic even further.

Learn other players’ tactics, refine your own, and challenge them again.

Put your logic to the test against the world.

Share Your Machine

Play a single Ranking Battle, and WORKSHOP unlocks.

Post the machine and logic you built and share it with players around the world.

Found a build that catches your eye? Download it and make it your own.

Wiring you never thought of. Machine builds you have never seen before.

Encounter the ideas Logickers around the world have built up, and sharpen your own logic even further.

How Would You Make It Fight?

Run rings around them with speed?

Push straight through with firepower?

Read their movements and meet them head-on?

Within limited parts and limited memory, find the answer that is yours alone.

You do not pilot. You design.

Entrust the tactics you devised to your robot.

That is SIGNOS: AI Robot Builder.

Key Features

  • Assemble “SIGNOS,” an 18cm-tall hobby robot

  • Design your machine around the performance of each part

  • Connect “Thought Tiles” to build behavior logic

  • Optimize your logic within a limited memory capacity

  • Fully automatic battles with no player input

  • A gameplay cycle of Design → Battle → Analyze → Improve

  • A Story Mode that takes you from the basics to advanced play (6 chapters)

  • Asynchronous Ranking Battles against other players’ AI

  • Share your machine and logic through WORKSHOP, unlocked after playing one Ranking Battle

  • Japanese / English / Simplified Chinese / Traditional Chinese / Korean / Thai / Spanish / Portuguese (Brazil) / German / French / Polish / Russian / Italian supported

SKEW is a first-person atmospheric exploration game about spaces that feel close to reality, yet quietly wrong.

Wander through liminal, dreamlike environments where structure begins to loosen, perspective feels uncertain, and familiar forms drift slightly out of place. Nothing breaks all at once. Instead, the world slips gradually, creating a constant sense of unease through stillness, scale, and silence.

There are no easy explanations waiting for you here. SKEW is less about being told what to feel, and more about letting you sit inside the feeling itself the tension of empty spaces, the weight of suspended moments, and the strange calm of a reality that no longer aligns with itself.

SKEW does not contain monsters, combat, or jump scares.
Its focus is on atmosphere, emotional tension, and environmental storytelling rather than horror.

Built around mood, visual composition, and surreal exploration, SKEW invites you into a journey suspended somewhere between memory, dream, and distortion.

Features

  • Explore surreal liminal spaces in first person

  • Experience a slow, immersive, atmospheric journey

  • No monsters, no combat, and no jump scares

  • Discover environments shaped by visual storytelling

  • Enter a world that feels familiar, yet subtly misaligned

Swing. Ram. Clear the stage.

An AI has taken control of the world’s machines. Choose from three tanks with distinct combat styles and take on its machine army.

Spin the turret, swing your cannon barrel, and ram straight through enemy ranks. Chain drifts, attacks, and each tank’s unique abilities to clear each stage.

More bosses and a wider variety of stages await in the full game.

Try SLAM TANK’s barrel-swinging action in the demo. The full game will bring more bosses and a wider variety of stages than the demo. Wishlist SLAM TANK to be notified when it launches.

 

 

Massive industrial machines block your path.

Dodge their attacks, close the gap, and chain barrel strikes with powerful abilities to fight back.

 

 

Hit boost pads to pick up speed, then launch off jump ramps.

Race across the battlefield, chaining drifts and mid-air tricks.

 

 

 

Smash machines - and the CPUs and GPUs inside them.

Your score is the total cost of the damage you deal to the AI’s machines.
Wreck more and beat your personal best.

 

 

Place decals and cosmetic parts wherever you like, then take your custom tank into battle.

From a single slime to an army that fills the battlefield.

Stack. Merge. Grow.


Bring slimes of the same tier together to merge them into bigger slimes. Fill your container with squishy, wobbling bodies and build a stronger army.

Open the gate. Unleash your army.


Keep merging, or release your army now? Open the gate and send your slimes pouring onto the battlefield. While they advance toward the enemy base, start stacking your next force.

Conquer new ground. Choose your growth.


Overcome enemy troops and boss attacks to reach new battlefields. Invest the Slime Essence, Biomass, and Conquest earned through merging, fighting, and conquering into permanent research for production, merging, and combat.

Return to the Demon Castle. Prepare your next push.


Spend time with the slimes living in your castle. Pick one up and give the crowd a playful shove to send slimes tumbling. Watch their squishy bodies bump and bounce, inspect your next stage, and prepare your research for the next push.

Your hands do different jobs

The moment a battle starts, notes begin falling down the left lane. Your right hand picks attacks, skills and defenses; your left hand keeps time. The rhythm is not a minigame on the side — it is the combat.
  • Combo sharpens every strike, and from 20 combo your basic attacks land as criticals
  • Gold notes refill the whole party's MP — the fuel for your skills
  • Orange notes are the beat of an incoming enemy attack. Parry cleanly and the blow barely lands
  • Purple notes are the cast beat of skills and ultimates. Nail the timing and they hit 1.4x harder
  • Fill the gauge and the party strikes as one in a joint Ultimate
If the rhythm is too much, turn on auto-hit in the settings. Notes are played for you, so the battle stays yours no matter your rhythm skill.

A den that changes as you dig

Fifty floors, split into five zones of ten. You start in a moss-choked dungeon and pass through webbed caves, a graveyard of the dead and an abyssal rift before reaching the Lich's throne. Each zone brings its own palette and music, and each ends with a boss whose signature move can only be blocked on rhythm.

Every floor offers a fork: the dangerous path thick with elites but heavy with treasure, the safe path with a guaranteed campfire, the merchant's path. You choose what to risk.

Four companions, thirteen paths

You name your party at the start. They begin as Novices, pick one of Warrior, Rogue, Mage or Priest at level 5, and branch again at 16 — whether yours becomes a Berserker or a Paladin depends on how you raised them.
  • 13 jobs, each with its own skills
  • 20 relics that change the rules rather than the numbers — count GOOD as PERFECT, strike twice with basic attacks, keep your combo through a MISS
  • Gear with affixes, consumables, merchants, campfires, gambling dens and training grounds

What death leaves behind

Even a wipe pays out: soul shards equal to the depth you reached. Spend them at the Soul Altar on permanent blessings, or break the seals on the most powerful relics. The next expedition starts a little stronger.

The Archive fills with the monsters you have met and the relics you have held, and keeps your fastest clear on every difficulty.
